hypotheses.justification: Summability still holds for arbitrary number fields, although the integral formula changes. Put σ = s.re, x = idealSetElement K J a, N = idealSetIntNorm K J a, and P = ∏ w, (w x)^2. The assumption-free lemmas norm_complexPlaceMellinGaussian and integral_totallyComplexGaussian_eq_prod give the norm integral as C·P^(-σ), with C independent of a. There is a constant c > 0 such that w x ≥ c for every a and w: fundamentalCone is defined using a bounded logarithmic fundamental domain (ZSpan.fundamentalDomain_isBounded), and logMap_apply bounds log(w x) − log(N)/[K:ℚ]. The omitted place is bounded using the weighted product formula. Here N ≥ 1 by idealSetIntNorm_ne_zero, so log(N) ≥ 0. Consequently, InfinitePlace.prod_eq_abs_norm gives P = N·∏(w real), w x ≥ N·c^(nrRealPlaces K). Thus the integrals are bounded by a constant times N^(-σ), whose series is summable by summable_idealSet_inverseNormPower; apply Summable.of_norm_bounded. All bases are positive by idealSetElement_ne_zero, so no zero/junk-power cases arise. Empty indexing sets are harmless, and the logarithmic argument also covers unit rank zero.
